## sh-codemod package

## Classes

<table><thead><tr><th>

Class


</th><th>

Description

<tbody><tr><td>

[EditOverlapError](./sh-codemod.editoverlaperror.md)


</td><td>

Thrown by `apply()` when two accumulated edits claim the same text, so no output could honor both.

It exists so a caller can tell "my edits conflict" from every other failure, and can see which edits conflict. An edit set that conflicts never yields output: silently choosing a winner would corrupt the file in a way no later check could attribute.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[ForeignNodeError](./sh-codemod.foreignnodeerror.md)


</td><td>

Thrown by an editor's `replaceNode` and `insertBefore` when the node did not come from that editor's own parse.

A node's position is only meaningful against the text it was parsed from. Applying a node from another parse (or a `structuredClone` of one, which keeps its stale offsets) would edit whatever happens to sit at those offsets in this text, so it is refused up front.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[FormatSyntaxError](./sh-codemod.formatsyntaxerror.md)


</td><td>

Thrown by `format` when input is invalid shell or cannot be formatted without losing content.

It exists so callers can distinguish input that cannot be safely formatted from other failures and can point at the problem, without depending on how `sh-ast` reports parse failures. Formatting never returns partial output: a syntax error always surfaces as this error, never as text.

`offset`<!-- -->, `line` and `column` are measured in the input string the caller passed, using the same UTF-16 units as ESLint locations, so they index that string directly even when it holds multibyte characters. `byteOffset` is the parser's own UTF-8 offset, kept for tools that address the source as bytes.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[InvalidNodeError](./sh-codemod.invalidnodeerror.md)


</td><td>

Thrown by an editor's `replaceNode` and `insertBefore` when the argument is not a syntax node at all (for example `undefined` from a failed lookup).

TypeScript callers cannot reach it; it exists so a JavaScript caller gets a named, actionable failure rather than an incidental `TypeError` from inside the editor.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

## Functions

Function

Description

<tbody><tr><td>

[createEditor(text, options)](./sh-codemod.createeditor.md)


</td><td>

Starts an editing session over `text`<!-- -->: parse once, queue edits against nodes, apply them as plain text patches. Nothing is reprinted, so everything outside the edited node ranges (comments, whitespace, `\r\n`<!-- -->, multibyte characters) comes back byte for byte.

Ordering is defined so output never depends on accident: - Edits are placed by position in the original text, not by the order they were queued. - Edits that only touch (one ends where the next begins) are both applied. - Insertions at one position appear in the order `insertBefore` was called. - An insertion at the start of a replaced node comes before the replacement; an insertion at its end comes after it. - Anything else that shares text, including two replacements of one node or an insertion strictly inside a replaced node, makes `apply()` throw [EditOverlapError](./sh-codemod.editoverlaperror.md)<!-- -->.

The result is not re-parsed; a caller who needs to know it is still valid shell can parse it.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[format(text, options)](./sh-codemod.format.md)


</td><td>

Formats shell source into the canonical text of mvdan/sh's printer (the `shfmt` style).

The text is parsed and printed through `sh-ast`<!-- -->, so the result is determined by the AST alone: layout, blank-line runs and `\r\n` line endings in the input do not survive, while comments and here-document bodies do. Formatting is idempotent.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

<tr><td>

[FormatOptions](./sh-codemod.formatoptions.md)


</td><td>

Options for `format`<!-- -->: producer-native grammar values, diagnostic filename, and public printer knobs. The parser alone decides which numeric variants it accepts.

Only the parse options that cannot change what is printed are exposed. `RecoverErrors` would let malformed input through as a repaired tree, and `StopAt` would silently drop the rest of the file; both break the guarantee that formatting never loses or invents code. `KeepComments` is not exposed either: comments are always kept (except under `Minify`<!-- -->, which omits them by definition).


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[TextEdit](./sh-codemod.textedit.md)


</td><td>

One text replacement: the half-open UTF-16 `range` of the original text that `text` takes the place of. An insertion is a replacement whose range is empty.


</td></tr>
